q: Google News 首版功能范围包括哪些？（多选）
q_en: Which features belong in the first version of Google News? (Select all that apply.)
options: 聚合展示来自大量发布方的新闻 feed
支持无限滚动加载更多文章
点击文章后跳转到发布方网站阅读全文
首版就要支持收藏、分享和按兴趣定制
options_en: Show an aggregated feed of articles from many publishers.
Support infinite scroll to load more articles.
Let users click through to read the full article on the publisher's site.
Ship saving, sharing, and interest-based personalization in v1.
why: 首版只做聚合 feed、无限滚动和跳转阅读；收藏、分享、兴趣定制都放在后续版本。
why_en: The v1 scope is an aggregated feed, infinite scroll, and click-through to publishers, leaving personalization and sharing for later.
optionExplanations: 聚合 feed 是产品的核心骨架，没有它后面的分页、缓存、排序都无从谈起。
无限滚动决定了分页策略要能撑住连续加载，避免用户翻页时卡顿或重复。
跳转阅读省去了平台托管全文的版权和存储负担，把内容责任留在发布方那边。
收藏、分享和个性化排序会把范围一下子扩大到用户画像和长期存储，首版先不做，把复杂度往后推。
optionExplanations_en: This is the product's core skeleton: a merged feed pulled from many sources, without which there's nothing downstream to paginate, cache, or rank.
Continuous-loading UX forces the pagination strategy to hold up as users keep pulling more pages instead of breaking on repeats.
Sending readers to the publisher's site keeps the platform out of hosting full article text and the copyright load that comes with it.
Saving, sharing, and personalized ranking would pull in user profiling and long-term storage right away, so v1 defers that complexity.

scenario: 新闻平台在分区或依赖抖动时需要做 CAP 取舍，用户更能接受看到稍旧新闻，而不是 feed 完全不可用。
scenario_en: During partitions or dependency hiccups, the news platform must make a CAP tradeoff: users would rather see slightly stale news than no feed at all.
q: 首要应该偏向 CAP 的哪一侧？
q_en: Which side of CAP should the first design favor?
options: 强一致优先，宁可返回错误也不能旧
可用性优先，允许短时间旧内容
事务隔离优先，所有 feed 请求串行化
完全实时优先，每次都绕过缓存查源
options_en: Favor strong consistency, even if that means returning an error instead of stale data.
Favor availability, accepting slightly stale content for a short time.
Favor transaction isolation, serializing every feed request.
Favor full real-time reads, bypassing the cache on every request.
why: 新闻 feed 不是金融扣款，短暂旧内容比空白页更可接受，因此偏向可用性。
why_en: A news feed should favor availability over strict consistency because slightly stale content beats showing nothing at all.
whenOtherWins: 如果系统处理账户余额、库存扣减或合规审计，强一致会比可用性更重要。
tradeoff: 可用性优先 vs 强一致优先

termDefinitions.meaning: CAP 定理说明分布式系统在网络分区时只能在一致性和可用性之间二选一。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The CAP theorem says a distributed system must choose between consistency and availability during a network partition.

optionExplanations: 只有在做账户余额、库存扣减或合规审计这类不容许出错的写场景时，才值得为一致性放弃可用性。
新闻 feed 的用户宁可看到几秒前的旧内容，也不想看到空白或错误页，短暂陈旧换持续可用是对的取舍。
串行化所有请求会把读吞吐压到远低于新闻场景需要的水平，事务隔离也不是这里要解决的问题。
每次绕过缓存直接查源，会让延迟和数据库压力一起失控，新闻场景不需要这种强实时。
optionExplanations_en: Strong consistency only earns its keep on writes that truly cannot tolerate an error, like account balances, inventory deductions, or compliance audits.
News readers would rather see content from a few seconds ago than a blank or error page, so trading brief staleness for uptime is the right call here.
Serializing every request would crater read throughput far below what a news feed needs, and transaction isolation isn't the axis this problem tests.
Bypassing the cache on every read lets latency and database load spiral together, which this feed doesn't need real-time freshness to justify.

scenario: 为新闻聚合器设计数据模型，用户可以匿名浏览，feed 按地区展示。
scenario_en: You are designing the data model for a news aggregator where users can browse anonymously and feeds are shown by region.
q: 新闻聚合器的数据模型需要先对齐哪些核心实体？（多选）
q_en: Which core entities should the news aggregator data model define first? (Select all that apply.)
options: Article：标题、摘要、发布时间、发布方和地区
Publisher：新闻来源、站点 URL、feed 地址和地区
User：至少有 id 和地区，用于生成区域 feed
Payment：用于订阅收费和账单结算
options_en: Article: title, summary, publish time, publisher, and region.
Publisher: source name, site URL, feed address, and region.
User: at minimum an id and region, used to build the regional feed.
Payment: used for subscription billing and settlement.
why: Article 是内容，Publisher 是来源，User 的地区决定 feed；支付不在本题范围。
why_en: Article, Publisher, and User are the core entities because they represent content, source, and the regional feed context, while payment is out of scope.
optionExplanations: Article 承载标题、摘要、发布方和地区这些展示字段，是 feed 里真正被渲染的内容单元。
Publisher 记录来源站点和 feed 地址，采集流水线要靠它才知道去哪里拉文章。
User 只需要 id 和地区两个字段，地区值直接决定这个用户该拿到哪个区域的 feed。
订阅计费属于支付子系统，跟聚合器首版要对齐的内容实体没有关系，不该混进数据模型。
optionExplanations_en: Article stores the headline, summary, where it came from, and which locale it belongs to — the piece actually rendered on a feed card.
Publisher records the source site and feed address, which the ingestion pipeline needs to know where to pull articles from.
User only needs an id and a region field, and that single value decides which local edition of the feed this reader sees.
Subscription billing belongs to a payments subsystem, unrelated to the content entities the aggregator needs to align on first.

scenario: 首版只需要让用户按地区拉取新闻 feed，先用最容易解释的分页接口，再在 deep dive 中优化。
scenario_en: The first version only needs to let users fetch a regional news feed with the simplest explainable pagination, then optimize it later.
q: 哪一个接口最贴合首版 feed API？
q_en: Which endpoint best matches the v1 feed API?
options: GET /feed?page={page}&limit={limit}&region={region}
POST /feed/rebuildAll?region={region}&async=true
GET /article/{id}/content?format=full&lang={lang}
POST /publisher/{id}/charge?amount={amount}&currency={cur}
options_en: GET /feed with page, limit, and region query params.
POST /feed/rebuildAll with a region and an async flag.
GET /article/{id}/content with a format and language param.
POST /publisher/{id}/charge with an amount and currency.
why: 首版接口只需按地区分页返回 Article；全文由浏览器跳到发布方站点，不由平台托管。
why_en: The v1 feed API only needs region and pagination because the full article is read on the publisher's own site.
whenOtherWins: 如果需要记录点击并训练推荐，可以再加一个 Google 自己的跳转跟踪端点。
tradeoff: 简单分页读接口 vs 托管全文/计费类接口
optionExplanations: 分页加地区两个参数就够客户端一页页拉 feed，是首版唯一需要的读接口。
全量重建缓存是运维触发的后台任务，不该挂在用户请求路径上，跟 feed 读取接口是两回事。
全文由发布方站点提供，平台不托管全文，这个接口对首版来说没有存在的理由。
首版功能范围里没有订阅计费，这个接口凭空引入了一个不存在的需求。
optionExplanations_en: Page and region are the only two params the client needs to pull the feed one page at a time — the only read endpoint v1 requires.
Rebuilding the whole cache is an ops-triggered background job, not something that belongs on the user-facing request path.
Full article text lives on the source site, not on our platform, so there's no reason for this endpoint to exist yet.
Subscription billing isn't part of the v1 scope, so this endpoint answers a need that doesn't exist yet.

q: 补全 RSS 在新闻聚合里的角色：
q_en: Fill in the role of RSS in news aggregation:
text: RSS 是发布方用来分发内容的 {{XML}} 格式，聚合器通过 {{HTTP GET}} 拉取 feed，再解析标题、链接和发布时间等元数据。
why: RSS 标准化、轻量、许多新闻站已支持，是默认的采集来源。
why_en: RSS is a lightweight, standardized XML format most news sites already support, making it the default ingestion source.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一种发布方用来分发文章元数据的 XML 格式，聚合器定期拉取。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: RSS is an XML syndication format publishers use to share article metadata that aggregators fetch periodically.

q: 把文章采集流水线按正确顺序排列：
q_en: Put the article ingestion pipeline in the right order:
steps: 把缩略图上传到对象存储，并把媒体 URL 写入文章元数据
从数据库读取发布方列表和 feed/API 地址
拉取 RSS/API 并解析文章元数据
下载原始媒体并生成适合 feed 的缩略图
why: 采集服务先找发布方，再拉取文章、处理媒体，最后把结构化数据和存储 URL 落库。
why_en: The collection job discovers publishers, fetches article metadata, processes media, then stores structured data with the object-storage URL.
diagram:
flowchart LR
RSS[RSS source] --> Fetch[Fetcher]
Fetch --> Parse[Parser]
Parse --> Dedup[Deduper]
Dedup --> DB[(Article DB)]
DB --> Cache[Feed cache]

termDefinitions.meaning: 面向大文件的存储服务，数据库只保存指向它的 URL。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Object storage holds large files like images while the database keeps only a URL pointing to them.

scenario: RSS 里有发布方图片 URL，feed 需要稳定、快速、尺寸一致地展示缩略图。
scenario_en: RSS contains publisher image URLs, but the feed needs thumbnails that are stable, fast, and consistently sized.
q: 为什么不直接把发布方图片 URL 原样交给客户端？
q_en: Why not send the publisher image URL directly to the client?
options: 发布方图片可能慢、失效或尺寸不统一
浏览器不能加载第三方图片
对象存储不能存图片
新闻平台必须托管全文
options_en: Publisher images can be slow, break, or come in inconsistent sizes.
Browsers are unable to load images hosted on a third-party domain.
Object storage is unable to hold image files.
A news platform must host full article text.
why: 自己下载、裁剪并存缩略图，能避开发布方服务器的可用性问题，也能统一展示质量。
why_en: Owning the thumbnail avoids depending on slow or broken publisher images and keeps display quality consistent.
whenOtherWins: 如果只是后台审核工具、流量很小且不关心展示一致性，直接引用外部图片更省事。
tradeoff: 自建缩略图的稳定可控 vs 直接引用节省的采集成本

termDefinitions.meaning: 面向大文件（图片、视频）的存储服务，和数据库分开。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Object storage is a file store for large binaries like images, kept separate from the database.

optionExplanations: 对，发布方服务器不受我们控制，图片可能慢、挂掉或尺寸参差不齐，这才是要自己托管缩略图的原因。
这是个假设错误——跨域加载第三方图片在浏览器里完全可行，技术上没有这个限制。
对象存储恰恰是为图片这类二进制文件设计的，不存在存不了图片的问题。
全文托管是另一件事，聚合器本身不托管全文，跟这里要不要自建缩略图无关。
optionExplanations_en: Right — publisher servers are outside our control, and images can be slow, break, or come in mismatched sizes, which is exactly why we host our own thumbnails.
That's a false premise: browsers load cross-origin images all the time, there's no technical block here.
Object storage is built precisely for binaries like images, so this isn't a real limitation.
Hosting full article text is a separate question, and the aggregator doesn't do that anyway — it has nothing to do with owning thumbnails.

q: Feed Service 和 Data Collection Service 为什么要拆成两个服务？
q_en: Why split Feed Service from Data Collection Service?
options: 一个面向用户低延迟读，一个后台批量写入采集
两者必须用不同编程语言
Feed Service 只能访问对象存储
Data Collection Service 必须在客户端运行
options_en: One serves low-latency user reads, the other runs background batch ingestion writes.
The two services must be written in different programming languages.
Feed Service is only allowed to talk to object storage.
Data Collection Service must run inside the client app.
why: 两者的流量模型、更新频率和运维需求完全不同，拆开后能各自独立扩容。
why_en: The two services have very different traffic patterns and operational needs, so splitting them lets each scale independently.
tradeoff: 读路径低延迟扩容 vs 写路径批量吞吐扩容
optionExplanations: 对，两者流量模式完全不同——一个要扛低延迟读峰值，一个做后台批量写入，拆开后才能各自独立扩容。
编程语言选型跟服务边界怎么划完全是两件事，语言可以相同也不影响拆分。
这把访问权限当成了拆分理由，但 Feed Service 实际主要查的是缓存和数据库，不是对象存储。
这里把部署位置说反了，Data Collection Service 本就该是后台服务，不会跑在客户端。
optionExplanations_en: Right — one side has to absorb low-latency read spikes while the other churns through batch ingestion writes, and treating them as separate services means capacity decisions for one don't block the other.
Language choice is unrelated to where the service boundary sits; both could be written in the same language and the split would still make sense.
This treats access scope as the reason for splitting, but Feed Service mainly queries the cache and database, not object storage.
This gets the deployment location backwards — Data Collection Service is meant to run as a backend job, not inside the client.

q: 把用户读取 feed 的基础路径按顺序排列：
q_en: Put the basic user feed read path in order:
steps: Feed Service 查询某地区最近文章并按发布时间排序
客户端请求 /feed?region=US&limit=20
API Gateway 做路由、限流和校验
Feed Service 格式化 Article 列表并返回
why: 读路径从客户端进网关，再到 Feed Service 查询缓存并格式化响应。
why_en: The read path flows from client to gateway to the feed service, which queries the cache and formats the response.
diagram:
flowchart LR
User[User] --> Feed[Feed Service]
Feed --> Redis[(Regional Redis)]
Redis --> Article[Article metadata]
Feed --> Client[Feed response]

termDefinitions.meaning: 统一入口层，负责路由、限流和请求校验。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An API gateway routes requests and applies rate limiting and validation at the edge.

q: 在新闻不断插入 feed 顶部时，OFFSET/LIMIT 分页最典型的问题是什么？
q_en: When new stories keep landing at the top of the feed, what is the main OFFSET/LIMIT problem?
options: 用户可能看到重复文章或漏掉文章
客户端无法传 limit
数据库不能按发布时间排序
分页会禁止缓存
options_en: Users can see duplicate articles or miss some entirely.
The client is unable to pass a limit parameter.
The database cannot sort results by publish time.
Pagination makes caching impossible.
why: 新文章插入顶部会让后续页的 offset 边界移动，翻页时就会重复或跳过内容。
why_en: New articles inserted at the top shift the offset boundary for later pages, so users see duplicates or gaps.
optionExplanations: 对，新文章插进顶部会让 offset 边界跟着漂移，翻页时就会看到重复或漏掉的文章。
limit 参数本身传递没有任何问题，这跟 offset 漂移完全是两回事。
按发布时间排序的能力不受影响，问题出在 offset 会随插入移动，不是排序做不到。
分页机制不会阻止缓存，二者互不冲突。
optionExplanations_en: Right — every fresh story that appears above where the reader currently is knocks the page marker out of alignment, so later requests come back with repeats or holes.
Passing a limit parameter works fine; that's unrelated to why offset drifts.
Sorting by publish time still works — the issue is the offset shifting under inserts, not a sorting limitation.
Pagination doesn't block caching at all; the two aren't in conflict.

scenario: 用户已经拿到第一页新闻，之后有新文章插入顶部，但继续下滑不应受影响。
scenario_en: A user has loaded the first page, new articles may arrive at the top, and continued scrolling should not be affected.
q: 比 page/offset 更适合的分页方式是什么？
q_en: What pagination style fits better than page/offset here?
options: 随机跳页
基于最后一条发布时间的 cursor
每次重新返回第一页
把所有文章一次性发给客户端
options_en: Jump to a random page number.
A cursor anchored on the timestamp of the last item.
Always return page one again.
Send every article to the client in one response.
why: cursor 固定在上一页最后一条的时间边界，新文章不会移动旧内容窗口。
why_en: A timestamp cursor anchors to a fixed boundary, so newly inserted articles never shift the older results.
whenOtherWins: 如果数据集很小且几乎不变，offset 分页更简单也够用。
tradeoff: 稳定边界的 cursor 分页 vs 实现更简单的 offset 分页
optionExplanations: 跳页依赖的页码本身就是漂移的根源，插入新文章后页码和内容根本对不上。
对，cursor 锚定在上一页最后一条的时间戳上，不管顶部插入多少新文章，这条边界都不会被推移。
每次都重回第一页等于放弃增量加载，用户会不停看到同样的开头内容，翻不到后面。
一次性把全部文章发给客户端，响应体和内存都会随文章数增长直接炸掉。
optionExplanations_en: Jumping by page number is itself the source of drift — the page number no longer lines up with content once new articles are inserted.
Right — anchoring on the timestamp of the last item on the page gives a fixed marker that new arrivals at the top can't push around.
Always returning page one abandons incremental loading; the user keeps seeing the same opening articles and never reaches the rest.
Sending every article in one response blows up both payload size and memory as the article count grows.

q: 只用 published_at 作为 cursor 时，多个文章同一时间发布会带来什么风险？
q_en: What can go wrong if the cursor uses only published_at and several articles share the same timestamp?
options: 相同时间戳边界上的部分文章可能被跳过
所有文章的一致性级别都会自动变成强一致
这张表原有的数据库索引将无法建立
客户端完全没有能力解析这种时间格式
options_en: Articles that share the exact cursor timestamp can be skipped.
The consistency level of every article automatically becomes strongly consistent.
The database index that already existed on this table becomes impossible to build.
The client has no ability whatsoever to parse this kind of timestamp format.
why: 下一页查询用 published_at < cursor 时，相同时间戳但还没返回的文章会被漏掉。
why_en: Querying with published_at less than the cursor excludes articles that share that exact timestamp but were not yet returned.

termDefinitions.meaning: 分页用的稳定定位标记，通常是上一页最后一条记录的排序字段值。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A cursor is a stable pagination marker, usually the sort-key value of the last item on the previous page.

optionExplanations: 对，只按发布时间小于 cursor 过滤时，卡在同一个(published_at)时间戳、还没轮到返回的文章就会被漏掉。
一致性级别跟这个风险完全无关，cursor 碰撞不会让数据变强一致。
时间戳字段完全可以建索引，问题出在值本身会重复，不是索引能力。
时间格式解析不是这里的障碍，风险在于多篇文章共享同一个值。
optionExplanations_en: Right — a strict less-than filter on that timestamp column drops any article sitting at the exact same value that hasn't been served yet.
Consistency level has nothing to do with this risk; timestamp collisions don't make data strongly consistent.
The timestamp column can absolutely be indexed; the problem is duplicate values, not indexing capability.
Parsing the timestamp format isn't the obstacle here — the risk is several articles sharing one value.

scenario: 多个新闻源批量导入文章，许多文章发布时间完全相同，无限滚动必须稳定不漏数据。
scenario_en: Many publishers batch-import articles with identical publish times, and infinite scroll must stay stable without missing items.
q: 最稳的 cursor 设计是什么？
q_en: What is the most stable cursor design?
options: 沿用容易在插入新文章时漂移的 page number
只用 region 字段作为文章间的排序依据
组合 published_at + article_id 做全序
只用容易重复、非唯一的文章标题排序
options_en: Stick with page numbers, which drift whenever new articles are inserted.
Use only the region field as the ordering key between articles.
Combine published_at and article_id into a total order.
Sort by article title, which is often duplicated and not unique.
why: 时间戳加唯一 ID 能在相同时间戳内继续打破平局，形成稳定的总排序。
why_en: Pairing the timestamp with a unique article ID breaks ties within the same timestamp and gives a stable total order.
whenOtherWins: 如果一开始就用严格单调递增的文章 ID，单 ID cursor 更简单。
tradeoff: 组合游标的稳定全序 vs 单字段游标的实现简单
optionExplanations: 沿用页码等于把漂移问题原样搬进批量导入场景，批量入库时问题只会更明显。
region 字段只用来分组，同地区文章之间的先后顺序完全没被定义。
对，时间戳加上唯一 ID 能在同一时间戳内继续区分先后，形成稳定的总排序，专门解决批量导入的碰撞。
标题经常重复又不唯一，拿它当排序键会让结果顺序不确定。
optionExplanations_en: Sticking with page numbers just carries the drift problem straight into batch imports, where it only gets worse.
Region only groups articles; it defines no order between articles that share the same region.

Right — tacking each row's distinct id onto that same publish-time value erases any tie occurring at that identical moment, producing one dependable ordering built for exactly this batch-import collision.
Titles repeat often and aren't unique, so sorting by them leaves the result order undetermined.

scenario: 系统从设计初期就能控制文章 ID 策略，希望无限滚动查询尽量简单高效。
scenario_en: The system can control article ID generation from the start and wants infinite-scroll queries to stay simple and efficient.
q: 哪种查询最适合单调递增 article_id cursor？
q_en: Which query best fits a monotonically increasing article_id cursor?
options: WHERE article_id < :cursor ORDER BY article_id DESC LIMIT 20
SELECT * FROM articles OFFSET :page * :limit LIMIT 20
SELECT * FROM articles WHERE title LIKE :cursor LIMIT 20
SELECT * FROM articles ORDER BY RANDOM() LIMIT 20
options_en: WHERE article_id < cursor ORDER BY article_id DESC LIMIT 20.
SELECT star FROM articles OFFSET page times limit, LIMIT 20.
SELECT star FROM articles WHERE title LIKE cursor, LIMIT 20.
SELECT star FROM articles ORDER BY RANDOM(), LIMIT 20.
codeSample:
SELECT *
FROM articles
WHERE region = $1 AND article_id < $2
ORDER BY article_id DESC
LIMIT 20;
why: 单调 ID 天然给文章唯一顺序，查询只需简单范围扫描加倒序索引。
why_en: A monotonically increasing article ID turns feed pagination into a simple indexed range scan.
whenOtherWins: 如果已大量使用随机 UUID 且无法迁移，组合时间戳和 ID 的 cursor 更现实。
tradeoff: 单调 ID 的查询简单 vs 组合游标的迁移灵活
optionExplanations: 对，单调 ID 只要做范围过滤加倒序，就能走索引扫描，天然适合这种 cursor 设计。
按页码算跳过的行数，翻得越深扫描的行越多，越翻越慢，也没解决漂移问题。
cursor 存的是 ID 不是标题，拿标题做模糊匹配语义上就用错了字段。
完全随机排序连基本的可重复分页顺序都保证不了，没法用来分页。
optionExplanations_en: Right — filtering on article_id and sorting it backwards compiles down to a scan that walks a single index in order, exactly what a monotonic-id cursor is built for.
Computing rows to skip by page number gets slower the deeper you page, and it still doesn't fix drift.
The cursor holds an id, not a title, so matching it against a title with LIKE is using the wrong field entirely.
Fully random ordering can't even guarantee a repeatable sequence across pages, so it can't support pagination at all.

q: 补全高效 cursor 查询需要的索引：
q_en: Fill in the indexes needed for efficient cursor queries:
text: 如果 cursor 使用发布时间和文章 ID，总查询通常需要 {{(published_at, article_id)}} 的组合索引；如果只用单调文章 ID，则需要 {{article_id}} 上的索引。
why: cursor 只有配合排序字段上的索引，才能避免每页扫描大量历史文章。
why_en: Cursor pagination only stays fast when there is an index on the same fields used for ordering.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在多个列上联合建立的索引，用来支撑组合排序或过滤查询。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A composite index spans multiple columns to support combined sort or filter queries.

scenario: 100M DAU 每天多次刷新 feed，直接按地区查数据库很难稳定低于 200ms。
scenario_en: With 100M DAU refreshing the feed multiple times per day, direct regional database reads are hard to keep under 200 ms.
q: 第一步最自然的低延迟优化是什么？
q_en: What is the most natural first step for lower feed latency?
options: 把最近文章按地区缓存在 Redis
把每个请求写入 Kafka 后再返回
禁用分页
把图片二进制放进数据库
options_en: Cache recent articles per region in Redis.
Write every request into Kafka before responding.
Disable pagination entirely.
Store image binaries inside the database.
why: 新闻消费远多于写入，按地区缓存热点 feed 能把大多数读请求从数据库转到内存。
why_en: News reads vastly outnumber writes, so caching hot regional feeds moves most reads from disk to memory.
whenOtherWins: 如果每个用户看到完全不同且强实时的内容，简单地区缓存命中率会下降。
tradeoff: 内存缓存降延迟 vs 陈旧和失效复杂度
optionExplanations: 对，新闻场景里读的次数远超写入，把各地区的热门 feed 放进内存，大部分读请求就能从磁盘查询转向直接命中缓存。
把请求写进 Kafka 解决的是异步处理和削峰，不是读路径的延迟问题。
分页本身不是延迟根源，禁用它只会让单次响应体变大，延迟反而更差。
大二进制文件塞进结构化数据库会拖慢核心元数据查询和备份，图片不该存在这里。
optionExplanations_en: Right — news gets read far more than it's produced, so keeping each area's popular stories in Redis pulls the bulk of that traffic off disk and into RAM.
Writing every request into Kafka solves async processing and buffering spikes, not read-path latency.
Pagination isn't the source of latency; disabling it only makes each response bigger, which makes latency worse.
Stuffing large binaries into a structured database drags down core metadata queries and backups — images don't belong there.

q: 用 30 分钟 TTL 的 cache-aside 区域 feed，主要会带来哪两个问题？
q_en: What are the two main problems with a 30-minute TTL cache-aside regional feed?
options: 内容可能最长半小时不新，过期时还可能出现缓存击穿
Redis 会自动执行 SQL join
数据库写入会完全停止
客户端不能再无限滚动
options_en: Content can be stale for up to 30 minutes, and expiry can trigger a thundering herd.
Redis starts automatically executing SQL joins.
Database writes stop completely.
The client can no longer support infinite scroll.
why: TTL 缓存能降读压，但新闻新鲜度差；同一地区缓存过期时大量请求可能同时打库。
why_en: A TTL cache reduces read load but hurts freshness, and when a regional entry expires many requests can hit the database at once.

termDefinitions.meaning: 应用先查缓存，未命中时查数据库并回填缓存。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Cache-aside checks the cache first and fills it from the database on a miss.
TTL is the time after which a cached entry expires and must be refreshed.

optionExplanations: 对，TTL 内内容可能滞后到快半小时，缓存到期那一刻还可能出现大量请求同时打库的击穿。
Redis 不具备执行 SQL join 的能力，这个说法本身就不成立。
缓存策略跟数据库写入路径互不影响，写入不会因为加了 TTL 缓存就停下来。
无限滚动是分页机制的事，跟缓存策略是两条独立的逻辑。
optionExplanations_en: Right — content can sit stale for up to 30 minutes, and the instant one region's entry lapses, a burst of traffic can converge on the backing store all at once.
Redis has no ability to run SQL joins; that claim isn't even technically true.
Caching strategy doesn't touch the write path at all — writes keep flowing regardless of a TTL cache.
Infinite scroll is a pagination concern, a separate piece of logic from caching strategy.

scenario: feed 要同时满足新文章快速出现和稳定低延迟，不想等 TTL 过期才刷新缓存。
scenario_en: The feed must show new articles quickly while staying low latency, without waiting for TTL expiry to refresh the cache.
q: 更好的缓存更新方式是什么？
q_en: What is the better way to update the feed cache?
options: 每天凌晨用批处理任务全量重建缓存
CDC 事件触发 worker 增量更新 Redis
让客户端自己定时轮询发布方 RSS 内容
每次收到请求都先清空缓存再查库
options_en: Rebuild the entire cache once every night with a batch job.
Use CDC events to trigger a worker that updates Redis incrementally.
Have the client poll publisher RSS feeds on its own schedule.
Clear the cache on every single request before querying the database.
why: 新文章入库后由 CDC 驱动 worker 更新对应地区 sorted set，兼顾新鲜度和命中率。
why_en: CDC-driven workers update the regional sorted set right after an article is written, keeping the feed fresh without sacrificing hit rate.
whenOtherWins: 如果写入极少且新鲜度要求很低，简单 TTL cache-aside 的运维成本更低。
tradeoff: CDC 实时刷新 vs TTL 定时刷新的运维简单
diagram:
flowchart LR
DB[(Article DB)] --> CDC[CDC stream]
CDC --> Builder[Feed builder]
Builder --> Redis[(Region feed cache)]
Redis --> Feed[Feed Service]

termDefinitions.meaning: 数据库变更捕获，把每次写入转成可被下游消费的事件。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: CDC turns each database write into an event that downstream workers can consume.

optionExplanations: 夜间批量重建的刷新粒度是一整天一次，新文章要等到下次重建才可见，新鲜度太粗。
对，CDC 事件在文章一入库就触发 worker 增量更新对应地区的 sorted set，新鲜度和命中率两头都兼顾了。
采集职责本就不该下放到客户端，客户端也没有能力稳定轮询成千上万个发布方源。
每次请求都先清空再查库，等于把缓存直接抵消掉了，跟不用缓存没区别。
optionExplanations_en: Rebuilding everything once overnight only refreshes daily, so new articles wait for the next rebuild to show up — too coarse.
Right — CDC events fire the moment an article lands, triggering a worker to update just that region's sorted set incrementally, keeping both freshness and hit rate.
Ingestion isn't the client's job, and it has no way to reliably poll thousands of publisher feeds on its own.
Wiping the cache before every single query cancels out the cache entirely — it's no better than having no cache at all.

scenario: Feed 已按地区预计算在 Redis sorted set 中，按发布时间倒序取第一页。
scenario_en: The feed is precomputed per region in a Redis sorted set, and the first page should read newest articles first.
q: 哪个 Redis 读法最贴合这个 feed 查询？
q_en: Which Redis read matches this feed query best?
options: ZREVRANGE feed:US 0 19
KEYS *
FLUSHALL
HGET publisher:US rss
options_en: ZREVRANGE feed:US 0 19.
KEYS star, scanning every key in the database.
FLUSHALL, wiping every key in Redis.
HGET publisher:US rss.
why: sorted set 用时间戳做 score，倒序范围读取能在毫秒级返回最新文章。
why_en: A sorted set scored by timestamp supports millisecond reverse-range reads for the newest articles.
whenOtherWins: 如果需要全文搜索或相关性排序，搜索引擎或推荐服务更合适。
tradeoff: sorted set 范围读的速度 vs 全文/相关性检索能力

termDefinitions.meaning: Redis 里按 score 排序的集合结构，可以做范围读取。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A sorted set is a Redis structure ordered by score that supports range reads.

optionExplanations: 对，sorted set 按 score 倒序取前 20 个成员，正好读出预计算好的最新一页 feed。
KEYS * 会扫描整个 keyspace，在生产环境是危险的全量扫描，不是取 feed 该用的命令。
FLUSHALL 会清空整个 Redis 实例的所有地区缓存，这是破坏性操作，不是读操作。
HGET 读的是发布方配置这个 hash 字段，拿不到文章列表，读的对象类型就不对。
optionExplanations_en: Right — reading the sorted set in reverse score order pulls exactly the newest 20 entries from the precomputed feed.
KEYS * scans the entire keyspace, a dangerous full scan in production, not the command for fetching a feed page.
FLUSHALL wipes every region's cache in the whole Redis instance — that's a destructive op, not a read.
HGET reads a hash field holding publisher config, not the article list — it's the wrong data type for this query.

scenario: 不再依赖 TTL，区域 feed cache 必须防止无限增长，只保留最近 1000-2000 篇。
scenario_en: Without relying on TTL, the regional feed cache must stay bounded and keep only the latest 1,000-2,000 articles.
q: 新增文章后应该配套哪类 Redis 清理操作？
q_en: After adding a new article, what Redis cleanup should run with it?
options: 每次插入一篇新文章都要执行一次 FLUSHDB 全部清空
ZADD 后用 ZREMRANGEBYRANK 裁掉最旧成员
直接用普通 SET 命令覆盖整个地区的全部数据
只增加一个 TTL 过期时间，完全不做任何裁剪操作
options_en: Run a full FLUSHDB wipe every single time one new article gets inserted.
ZADD the new article, then ZREMRANGEBYRANK to trim the oldest members.
Overwrite the entire region dataset directly with a plain SET command.
Only add a single TTL expiration and skip any trimming operation entirely.
why: CDC 更新后立即按 rank 裁剪，能让每个地区 cache 维持固定窗口，避免内存无界增长。
why_en: Trimming by rank right after each insert keeps every regional feed at a bounded window instead of growing forever.
whenOtherWins: 如果需要长期历史浏览，旧文章应落在数据库或搜索存储，而不是留在热 feed cache。
tradeoff: 裁剪保持内存可控 vs 保留完整历史可查
optionExplanations: 每次写入都清空整个数据库粒度太粗，代价太大，等于把所有地区缓存都清空重来。
对，写入新文章后立刻按排名删掉超额的旧成员，能让每个地区的集合大小稳定在固定窗口内。
普通 SET 命令会覆盖掉 sorted set 的排序结构，跟裁剪需要保留的有序集合语义不符。
本题已经不依赖 TTL 了，只设过期时间不做裁剪，集合还是会持续无限增长。
optionExplanations_en: Wiping the whole database per insert is way too blunt an operation — it blows away every region's cache just to land one article.
Right — running a rank-based trim immediately after ZADD caps each region's set at a fixed window so it never grows without bound.
A plain SET would overwrite the sorted set's ordered structure entirely, breaking the semantics trimming depends on.
This scenario already dropped TTL — adding an expiry without trimming still lets the set grow without bound.

scenario: 发布方暂时不支持推送，但重大新闻源需要在几分钟内被发现。
scenario_en: Publishers do not support push yet, but major news sources need to be discovered within a few minutes.
q: RSS 采集的合理改进是什么？
q_en: What is a reasonable improvement to RSS collection?
options: 所有发布方统一按每 6 小时一个周期轮询
高优先级源 5-10 分钟轮询，中低优先级放慢
永远只依赖人工手动逐条录入文章
不分主次，每秒都抓取所有发布方站点首页
options_en: Poll every publisher on the same flat six-hour schedule, no matter how often each one publishes.
Poll high-priority sources every 5-10 minutes and slow down the rest.
Rely permanently on someone manually typing in each article by hand.
Ignore priority entirely and scrape every publisher's homepage once every single second.
why: 按发布频率和重要性分层轮询，能把关键来源的发现延迟降到分钟级，同时控制成本。
why_en: Tiered polling gives major publishers minute-level freshness while keeping request volume for everyone else under control.
whenOtherWins: 如果发布方愿意集成 webhook，推送模式比高频轮询更快也更省资源。
tradeoff: 分层轮询兼顾新鲜度与成本 vs 统一节奏的简单实现
optionExplanations: 统一按六小时轮询，重大新闻要等好几个小时才会被发现，跟几分钟内要能发现的要求差太远。
对，把轮询频率按来源重要性分层，能让关键来源几分钟内被发现，同时不用把资源都花在低价值来源上。
人工录入没法支撑成千上万个发布方的规模，靠不住也扩展不了。
每秒抓取全部站点首页会让请求量暴涨，很容易被目标站点封禁。
optionExplanations_en: A flat six-hour cycle for the whole publisher list means big stories sit undiscovered for hours, nowhere near the few-minutes bar this needs.
Right — tiering poll frequency by source importance gets key publishers found within minutes without burning budget on low-value ones.
Manual entry can't scale to thousands of publishers; it's neither reliable nor a growth path.
Scraping every homepage once a second makes outbound traffic explode and risks getting the crawler blocked by target sites.

q: 高频 RSS 轮询时，哪些机制能减少无效处理或重复文章？（多选）
q_en: During frequent RSS polling, which mechanisms reduce wasted work or duplicate articles? (Select all that apply.)
options: 使用 ETag 或 Last-Modified 判断 feed 是否变化
用 GUID 或发布时间和 URL 识别新文章
不管 feed 是否变化都全量入库
按发布方历史频率设置轮询优先级
options_en: Use ETag or Last-Modified to check whether the feed actually changed.
Use the GUID, or publish time plus URL, to identify new articles.
Ingest the full feed every time regardless of whether it changed.
Set polling priority based on each publisher's historical frequency.
why: 条件请求、去重标识和优先级调度能让高频轮询更可控，避免重复处理和无意义带宽。
why_en: Conditional requests, dedupe identity, and priority scheduling keep frequent polling cheap and free of duplicate work.

termDefinitions.meaning: 服务器返回的内容指纹，客户端可用它判断内容是否变化。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An ETag is a content fingerprint the server returns so clients can tell whether content changed.

termDefinitions.meaning: 全局唯一标识符，这里用来判断 RSS 里的文章是否已处理过。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A GUID is a unique identifier used here to detect whether an RSS article was already processed.

optionExplanations: 条件请求能在 feed 没变化时直接跳过下载和解析，省掉整段无意义的网络和处理开销。
用 GUID 或时间加 URL 当唯一标识，能挡住同一篇文章被重复写入的风险。
不管内容是否变化都全量入库，白白浪费带宽和处理时间，正是要靠条件请求避免的问题。
按历史发布频率分配轮询优先级，能把有限的抓取预算花在真正高价值的来源上。
optionExplanations_en: Checking ETag or Last-Modified first lets a poll skip downloading and parsing entirely when nothing has changed, cutting out wasted work.
Using a GUID, or publish time plus URL, as identity blocks the risk of the same article getting written in twice.
Ingesting the full feed every single time wastes bandwidth and processing on content that never changed — the opposite of what this mechanism is for.
Setting poll priority by historical frequency spends a limited crawl budget on the sources that actually matter most.

scenario: 一些新媒体没有 RSS 或更新很慢，但平台仍希望覆盖它们的新文章。
scenario_en: Some digital publishers have no RSS or very slow RSS updates, but the platform still wants to cover their new articles.
q: 哪种补充采集方式最合适？
q_en: Which fallback ingestion method fits best?
options: 把这类发布方永久排除
用站点特定规则和指纹库做网页抓取
让用户上传新闻截图
只抓取图片不抓取文章链接
options_en: Permanently exclude these publishers from the platform.
Scrape with site-specific rules and a content fingerprint database.
Ask users to upload screenshots of the news.
Scrape only images and skip article links entirely.
why: 网页抓取能扫描首页和栏目页发现新链接，再用 URL hash 或内容校验和去重。
why_en: Targeted web scraping discovers new links from homepages and section pages, then dedupes using URL hashes or content checksums.
whenOtherWins: 如果站点提供稳定 RSS 或 webhook，优先用那些维护成本更低的标准接口。
tradeoff: 抓取扩大覆盖面 vs 维护成本和站点结构变化风险
optionExplanations: 直接排除这批发布方并不能解决覆盖率问题，只是回避了需求。
对，定制解析规则加内容指纹库，专门去爬没有 RSS 的站点前台页面和栏目列表，靠指纹去重挡住重复内容进库。
指望用户主动截图上传新闻不是可规模化的采集方式，靠不住也没法自动化。
文章链接本身才是核心数据，只抓图片跳过链接是把主次搞反了。
optionExplanations_en: Excluding these publishers outright doesn't solve the coverage gap, it just avoids the requirement.

Right — custom parsing rules paired with a content fingerprint store can crawl a site's front page and section listings for new links, catching duplicates by fingerprint instead of relying on feed metadata — exactly the gap RSS leaves.
Relying on users to voluntarily upload screenshots isn't a scalable ingestion method — it's unreliable and can't be automated.
Article links are the actual core data here; scraping only images and skipping links gets the priorities backwards.

scenario: 平台流量巨大，发布方愿意主动通知新文章，希望发布后几十秒内进 feed。
scenario_en: At very large traffic, publishers are willing to notify the platform, and new articles should enter the feed within tens of seconds.
q: 最优的采集模型是什么？
q_en: What is the best ingestion model?
options: 发布方不支持推送，只靠 6 小时一轮的 RSS 定时轮询
发布方 webhook 推送，RSS/抓取兜底
只在用户点开 feed 请求时才临时抓取一次
让 CDN 边缘节点自动发现并抓取新文章
options_en: Publishers don't support push, so lean entirely on RSS polling once every six hours.
Publisher webhooks push updates, with RSS and scraping as fallback.
Only scrape on demand, the moment a user actually opens the feed.
Let CDN edge nodes automatically discover and fetch new articles on their own.
why: webhook 把拉模式变成推模式，能在发布后几秒触发采集流水线；RSS 和抓取继续覆盖未集成的发布方。
why_en: Webhooks turn discovery into a push path that fires within seconds of publication, while RSS and scraping still cover non-integrated publishers.
whenOtherWins: 如果发布方没有技术资源或合作关系，系统只能依赖轮询和抓取。
tradeoff: webhook 推送的实时性 vs 轮询/抓取不依赖发布方配合

termDefinitions.meaning: 发布方主动调用平台接口推送事件，而不是被平台轮询。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A webhook lets the publisher push an event to our endpoint instead of us polling them.

optionExplanations: 六小时轮询的发现延迟停留在小时级，跟几十秒内要进 feed 的目标差了几个数量级。
对，让发布方主动推送事件，采集能在发布后几秒内启动，RSS 轮询和抓取继续给没接入推送的来源兜底。
等用户请求时才临时抓取，会让第一个访问的用户等很久，而且结果也不稳定。
CDN 只负责内容分发，本身不做内容发现，这个假设不成立。
optionExplanations_en: Six-hour polling keeps discovery latency at the hour level, orders of magnitude short of a tens-of-seconds target.

Right — a publisher-initiated notification flips discovery from pull to push, so ingestion starts moments after a story goes live; polling feeds and the scraping fallback still handle publishers that never wired one up.
Waiting to scrape until a user requests the feed makes the first visitor wait a long time, and the result is unreliable.
A CDN only distributes content, it doesn't discover new content — that assumption doesn't hold.

q: 把混合采集方案从最快到兜底的层次排列：
q_en: Order the hybrid ingestion layers from fastest to fallback:
steps: 没有 feed 或 feed 很差的站点用网页抓取补覆盖
合作发布方通过 webhook 主动推送新文章
有 RSS 的发布方按优先级轮询，条件请求和去重
新文章进入统一处理流水线并触发 feed cache 更新
why: webhook 最快，RSS 是标准拉取路径，抓取是覆盖兜底，最后都进入同一采集和缓存更新链路。
why_en: The hybrid stack favors webhooks first, RSS polling second, scraping as a coverage fallback, all feeding one downstream pipeline.
tradeoff: 推送实时性 vs 轮询/抓取的独立覆盖面

q: 把缩略图二进制直接存进文章数据库，主要后果是什么？
q_en: What is the main consequence of storing thumbnail bytes directly in the article database?
options: S3 会自动加速
所有图片都会免费 CDN 化
数据库查询、备份和内存使用都会被大对象拖慢
Feed Service 不再需要返回文章元数据
options_en: S3 automatically speeds up as a side effect.
Every image magically becomes CDN-distributed for free.
Large blobs slow down database queries, backups, and memory usage.
Feed Service no longer needs to return article metadata.
why: 数据库适合结构化元数据，不适合大量二进制 blob；图片会挤占缓存和 I/O，拖慢核心查询。
why_en: Databases are built for structured metadata, not binary blobs, and image data crowds out cache and I/O for core queries.
optionExplanations: 把图片存进数据库跟 S3 是否加速完全没关系，这个说法凭空捏造了因果。
CDN 分发需要单独接入和配置，不会因为图片存在数据库里就自动免费获得。
对，数据库是为结构化元数据设计的，塞进大量二进制会挤占缓存和 I/O，直接拖慢查询和备份。
Feed Service 该返回的元数据字段不受影响，图片存储方式改变不了这一点。
optionExplanations_en: Storing images in the database has nothing to do with whether S3 speeds up — this invents a cause that isn't there.
CDN distribution needs its own setup and integration; it doesn't happen for free just because images sit in the database.
Right — a relational store is meant to hold rows of structured fields, and packing it with large binaries crowds out the memory and disk bandwidth that core queries and backups both need.
The metadata fields Feed Service returns are unaffected — how images are stored doesn't change that.

scenario: 采集时需要保存 feed 缩略图，同时数据库只应保存结构化文章元数据。
scenario_en: During ingestion, the system must keep feed thumbnails while the database stores only structured article metadata.
q: 缩略图应如何存储？
q_en: How should thumbnails be stored?
options: 放进数据库 blob 字段
上传到对象存储，文章表只存 URL
只存在应用服务器本地磁盘
放进用户浏览器 localStorage
options_en: Store thumbnail bytes in a database blob column.
Upload to object storage, and store only the URL in the article table.
Keep thumbnails only on local application-server disk.
Save thumbnails inside the user's browser localStorage.
why: 对象存储负责文件本体，数据库只保存 URL 和元数据，职责清晰也更易扩展。
why_en: Object storage owns the file while the database keeps only the URL and metadata, keeping responsibilities clean and scalable.
whenOtherWins: 如果图片只是临时小文件且不会大规模访问，本地临时存储可用于处理过程但不能长期服务。
tradeoff: 对象存储的可扩展托管 vs 本地磁盘的零额外依赖
optionExplanations: 把图片字节塞进数据库表会重演大对象拖慢查询和备份的问题。
对，文件进对象存储、数据库只留 URL 引用，数据库保持轻量，文件本身也能独立扩展。
缩略图留在单台服务器磁盘，扩容出新实例后就找不到旧图片了，没法多实例共享。
浏览器 localStorage 不是服务端可控的存储，用户换设备或清缓存图片就没了。
optionExplanations_en: Putting image bytes into a database column would repeat the exact large-blob problem of slowing down queries and backups.
Right — a blob store owns the actual bytes while the articles table keeps just a pointer to it, so that table stays light and files scale on their own.
Keeping thumbnails on one server's local disk means a new instance can't find images from before it was spun up — nothing shared across instances.
Browser localStorage isn't storage the server controls; the image disappears the moment the user switches devices or clears cache.

scenario: 全球用户都要快速加载缩略图，单一区域对象存储回源会让远端用户延迟高、成本大。
scenario_en: Global users need thumbnails to load quickly, and going back to one-region object storage adds latency and origin cost.
q: 应该在对象存储前增加什么？
q_en: What should be added in front of object storage?
options: 在写路径上加一层关系型数据库触发器
把单个应用服务器规格升级得更大更强
CloudFront/CDN 边缘分发
让客户端自己定时轮询发布方 RSS 源
options_en: Add a relational database trigger somewhere in the write path.
Just upgrade the single application server to a bigger, beefier box.
A CloudFront-style CDN distributing content at the edge.
Have the client itself poll the publisher's RSS feed on a timer.
why: CDN 在边缘缓存缩略图，让全球用户就近命中，同时减少对源存储的直接请求。
why_en: A CDN caches thumbnails at edge locations so global users hit a nearby node instead of the origin storage.
whenOtherWins: 如果媒体只给内部低流量用户看，直接对象存储 URL 可能已经足够。
tradeoff: CDN 边缘命中降延迟 vs 直连对象存储的架构简单
diagram:
flowchart LR
Publisher[Publisher image] --> Proxy[Image proxy]
Proxy --> Blob[(Object storage)]
Blob --> CDN[Image CDN]
CDN --> Client[Client]
optionExplanations: 数据库触发器处理的是写入时的额外逻辑，跟图片怎么分发给全球用户完全不搭边。
垂直扩容单台服务器规格再高，也没有地理分布能力，解决不了跨大洲的延迟。
对，CDN 在全球边缘节点缓存缩略图，远端用户命中附近节点，延迟骤降，还能减少回源请求。
客户端轮询 RSS 是采集环节的事，跟图片加载延迟是两条不相关的路径。
optionExplanations_en: A database trigger runs extra logic on writes; it has nothing to do with how images get distributed to users worldwide.
A bigger single server, however beefed up, still has no geographic distribution — it can't fix cross-continent latency.

Right — fronting the source bucket with edge nodes means a reader on the other side of the planet lands on a nearby cache rather than round-tripping back to where the file actually lives, and load on that source drops too.
Client-side RSS polling belongs to ingestion, an unrelated path from image load latency.

q: 补全缩略图多尺寸策略：
q_en: Fill in the multi-size thumbnail strategy:
text: feed 可以生成 {{150x100}} 移动端、{{300x200}} 桌面端、{{600x400}} 高密屏等多个缩略图版本，再由客户端或 srcset 选择。
why: 多尺寸缩略图能让移动端不下载过大图片，也让高密屏保持清晰。
why_en: Multiple thumbnail sizes stop mobile clients from downloading oversized images while keeping high-density screens sharp.

scenario: 突发新闻导致某地区 1000 万并发用户刷新 feed，但新闻消费天然按地域聚集。
scenario_en: A breaking story causes 10M concurrent users in one region to refresh the feed, and news consumption is naturally regional.
q: 最合理的整体扩展思路是？
q_en: What is the most reasonable overall scaling approach?
options: 所有地区共用一个巨大 Redis 和一个巨大数据库
按地区部署和扩容 feed/cache 层
让发布方承担用户流量
关闭图片以外的所有内容
options_en: Share one giant Redis and one giant database across all regions.
Deploy and scale the feed and cache layer per region.
Push the user traffic burden onto the publishers.
Turn off everything except images.
why: 新闻流量高度地域化，区域部署能让本地热点独立扩容，不影响其他地区。
why_en: News traffic is inherently regional, so scaling per region lets a local spike grow without straining every other region.
whenOtherWins: 如果内容完全全球共享且地域差异很小，全局缓存加多区域复制可能更简单。
tradeoff: 区域独立扩容 vs 全局共享架构的实现简单
optionExplanations: 把所有地区流量压到同一套基础设施上，突发地区的热点会先把整个共享集群打爆，牵连其他地区。
对，新闻流量天然按地域聚集，按地区部署能让突发地区单独加机器扩容，不拖累其他地区。
发布方没有能力也没有义务承担平台自己的用户流量，这个责任主体放错了。
关掉核心功能是妥协而不是扩展方案，没有真正解决扩展性问题。
optionExplanations_en: Pooling every region into one shared Redis and database means a spike in one place saturates the whole cluster and slows every reader everywhere else too.

Right — since consumption clusters by geography anyway, giving each region its own deployment means a local surge can grab extra capacity on its own, leaving the rest of the map completely unaffected.
Publishers have neither the capacity nor the obligation to absorb the platform's own user traffic — that responsibility is misplaced.
Turning off core features is a concession, not a scaling plan, and doesn't actually solve the scaling problem.

scenario: Feed Service 是无状态服务，突发新闻时单机无法处理千万级连接。
scenario_en: Feed Service is stateless, and a single machine cannot handle tens of millions of connections during breaking news.
q: 应用层应该如何扩展？
q_en: How should the application layer scale?
options: 把所有用户请求固定路由到同一台机器
把 Redis 缓存整个换成数据库触发器机制
负载均衡后面水平扩容多个 Feed Service 实例
跳过应用层，让客户端应用直接查询数据库
options_en: Pin every single user request to that one same machine.
Rip out Redis entirely and replace it with a database trigger mechanism.
Scale out multiple Feed Service instances behind a load balancer.
Skip the application layer and let the client app query the database directly.
why: 无状态服务最适合水平扩容，自动伸缩组能按负载补充或回收实例。
why_en: A stateless service is the easiest thing to scale horizontally, with auto-scaling adding or removing instances by load.
whenOtherWins: 如果服务持有强会话状态，扩容前要先外置状态或做会话粘滞。
tradeoff: 无状态水平扩容 vs 单机垂直扩容的天花板
optionExplanations: 把所有请求钉在一台机器上，单机连接数上限很快会被突发流量打穿，违背了水平扩容的初衷。
数据库触发器不是承接千万级并发读请求的手段，跟 Redis 要解决的问题不在一个层面。
对，服务是无状态的，负载均衡后开多个实例，自动伸缩组就能按负载弹性增减，是标准扩容方式。
让客户端绕过应用层直接查数据库，等于把海量客户端直接暴露给数据库，丢掉了缓存和应用层保护。
optionExplanations_en: Pinning every request to one machine gets its connection ceiling blown through by a spike almost immediately, defeating the point of horizontal scaling.
A database trigger isn't a way to absorb tens of millions of concurrent reads — it operates at a different layer than what Redis solves.
Right — since the service is stateless, scaling out multiple instances behind a load balancer lets an autoscaling group add or remove capacity by load, the standard approach.
Letting the client query the database directly bypasses the application layer, exposing the database straight to massive client traffic with no cache or app-layer protection.

q: 突发新闻期间，为什么数据库不应该承接绝大多数 feed 读？
q_en: During breaking news, why should the database not serve most feed reads?
options: 这个数据库完全不能保存任何文章
Feed Service 完全无法访问 Redis 缓存
即使有索引，千万级并发读也会卡在 I/O、CPU 和连接池
对象存储会自动删除历史文章
options_en: This database is completely unable to store any articles.
Feed Service is completely unable to reach the Redis cache.
Even with indexes, ten-million-level concurrent reads bottleneck on I/O, CPU, and connection pools.
Object storage automatically deletes historical articles.
why: 预计算 cache 的目的就是把热点读从数据库卸载掉，让数据库只承担写入和少量 miss 流量。
why_en: The cache layer exists specifically to shield the database from massive hot-feed reads during traffic spikes.
optionExplanations: 数据库本就负责存储文章，这个说法直接反了。
Feed Service 正是靠 Redis 分流大部分读请求，这个假设不成立。
对，就算加了索引，千万级并发读照样会撞上单机数据库的 I/O、CPU 和连接池物理上限。
对象存储和数据库删不删历史文章是两回事，跟这里的问题无关。
optionExplanations_en: The database is exactly what stores articles — this claim has it backwards.
Feed Service relies on Redis to offload most reads; that assumption is false.
Right — even with indexes, tens of millions of concurrent reads still hit the physical ceiling of a single database's I/O, CPU, and connection pool.
Whether object storage retires old articles has nothing to do with who serves reads — the cache or the backing store.

scenario: 每个区域 feed 只有约 2000 篇热文章，但突发事件时 Redis 读 QPS 暴涨。
scenario_en: Each regional feed has only about 2,000 hot articles, but Redis read QPS spikes during a breaking event.
q: Redis 层的主要扩展手段是什么？
q_en: What is the main way to scale the Redis layer?
options: 把每条文章拆成一个数据库表
禁用 sorted set
优先加读副本分摊读请求
用单个 master 处理所有读写
options_en: Split every article into its own database table.
Stop using the sorted-set data structure.
Add read replicas first to spread out the read traffic.
Keep a single master instance handling all reads and writes.
why: 数据量很小，瓶颈是读吞吐而不是容量；读副本能把 feed 查询分散到多台 Redis。
why_en: The regional data set is tiny, so the bottleneck is read throughput, and read replicas spread queries across many Redis nodes.
whenOtherWins: 如果单个区域缓存内容巨大到单机放不下，再考虑按 key 分片。
tradeoff: 读副本扩展读吞吐 vs 分片解决容量瓶颈
optionExplanations: 把文章拆成数据库表是数据库层的手段，答非所问，本题问的是 Redis 怎么扩展。
sorted set 本身正是这里最合适的数据结构，禁用它反而丢掉了范围读取的优势。
对，这里数据量不大，真正卡住的是读吞吐而非容量，加几个只读副本就能把 feed 查询摊到多台机器上。
单 master 扛所有读写，突发流量下会先被读请求打满，完全没有解决扩展问题。
optionExplanations_en: Splitting articles into database tables is a database-layer move, off-topic here since the question is about scaling Redis.
The sorted set is exactly the right structure for this job; dropping it throws away the range-read advantage it provides.

Right — with only about 2,000 hot articles per region, storage was never the constraint; what caps things is how many reads you can serve per second, and bringing in more read-only copies fans that load out across many nodes.
A single master handling all reads and writes gets saturated by read traffic first during a spike — it doesn't solve the scaling problem at all.

scenario: 某地区突发新闻，1000 万并发用户同时请求 feed；单个 Redis 实例约能处理 10 万请求/秒。
scenario_en: In one region, breaking news drives 10M concurrent feed requests, while one Redis instance handles about 100K requests per second.
q: 这个量级最支持哪条 Redis 扩展判断？
q_en: What Redis scaling conclusion does this order of magnitude support?
options: 一个 Redis master 实例足够应付所有区域读流量
应该放弃 Redis 改成把所有请求打到数据库
读流量需要多个 Redis 读副本分摊，而不是一个实例扛住
Redis 实例数量和用户数无关，不需要跟着扩容
options_en: A single Redis primary instance can handle all regional read traffic.
Redis should be dropped in favor of sending every request to the database.
Read traffic needs many Redis read replicas instead of one instance carrying it all.
The number of Redis instances has nothing to do with user count and never needs to scale.
why: 1000万请求除以每实例约10万请求，量级在百个实例左右，读吞吐必须靠多副本分摊。
why_en: Roughly ten million requests over about a hundred thousand per instance means you need on the order of a hundred Redis read replicas.
optionExplanations: 1000 万请求除以单实例约 10 万请求/秒，缺口有两个数量级，单实例远远不够。
抛弃 Redis 改打数据库，会让数据库直接面对原本设计要靠 Redis 挡住的千万级读流量。
对，按这个量级换算大约需要上百个 Redis 实例分摊，读流量必须靠多副本而不是一个实例扛。
实例数量恰恰要跟用户量一起扩容，这里的除法关系已经说明了这一点。
optionExplanations_en: The 10M concurrent figure against the roughly 100K one box can serve leaves a two-order-of-magnitude gap — a single primary can't come remotely close.
Dropping Redis for the database would throw the exact ten-million-read load Redis was meant to absorb straight at the database.
Right — at this order of magnitude the math works out to roughly a hundred instances, so read traffic needs many replicas, not one instance carrying it all.
Instance count is precisely what should scale with user count — the division here is what shows that relationship.

q: 补全 Redis 主从读写路径：
q_en: Fill in the Redis primary-replica read/write path:
text: 新文章和 cache 更新写到 {{master}}，feed 读请求通过负载均衡分发到多个 {{read replicas}}；master 故障时可由 {{Sentinel}} 或托管服务提升副本。
why: 主写从读能提升读吞吐，副本提升机制能减少单点故障的影响。
why_en: A primary handles writes while replicas serve reads, and automatic promotion limits the impact of a single point of failure.

termDefinitions.meaning: Redis 的高可用组件，监控主节点并在故障时把副本提升为新主。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Redis Sentinel monitors the primary and automatically promotes a replica if it fails.

q: 只在数据库里加 category 列并实时查询 category feed，规模上最大的问题是什么？
q_en: At scale, what is the biggest problem with just adding a category column and querying category feeds in the database?
options: 用户无法选择地区
文章不能有标题
热门分类请求会变成大量重复数据库过滤查询
Redis sorted set 不能按时间排序
options_en: Users lose the ability to select a region.
Articles are no longer allowed to have a title.
Hot-category requests turn into a flood of repeated database filter queries.
Redis sorted sets are unable to sort by time.
why: 体育、政治等热点分类会产生大量相同过滤查询，直接打数据库会耗尽连接池和 CPU。
why_en: Hot categories like sports or politics repeat the same filter query at scale, exhausting connection pools and CPU on the database.
optionExplanations: 地区选择功能不受分类字段实现方式影响，两者互不干扰。
标题字段完全不受影响，这跟新增 category 列没有关系。
对，像体育、政治这种流量集中的分类，会反复触发同一条过滤 SQL，全落到数据库上会先把连接池和 CPU 拖垮。
sorted set 本就支持按 score（时间戳）排序，这个说法本身不成立。
optionExplanations_en: Region selection isn't affected by how the category field is implemented; the two are unrelated.
The title field is completely unaffected — that has nothing to do with adding a category column.

Right — a section that's currently trending, think a major sports final or a breaking election story, fires the exact same WHERE-category clause thousands of times over, and sending each one straight to the database burns through its connection budget and CPU headroom.
Sorted sets already support ordering by score, which is the timestamp here — that claim isn't even true.

scenario: 系统有 25 个分类和 10 个地区，希望 category feed 查询也低于 200ms。
scenario_en: The system has 25 categories and 10 regions, and category feed queries should also stay under 200 ms.
q: 一种可扩展但更复杂的方案是什么？
q_en: What is a scalable but more complex approach?
options: 放弃缓存，每次分类请求都重新扫描一遍全量文章数据表
只支持一个分类，其余分类全部下线不再对外提供服务
给 category-region 组合预建 sorted set
偷偷把 category 字段悄悄藏进图片文件名里蒙混过关
options_en: Drop the cache and rescan the entire article table from scratch on every category request.
Support just one category and take every other category fully offline.
Precompute a Redis sorted set for every category-region combination.
Quietly hide the category value inside the image filename to sneak past the design.
why: feed:sports:US 这类 sorted set 能把分类查询变成 Redis 范围读取，但会增加缓存键和维护复杂度。
why_en: Sorted sets like feed:sports:US turn category lookups into a Redis range read, at the cost of more cache keys to maintain.
whenOtherWins: 如果分类只用于轻量过滤，且区域缓存已包含足够文章，在内存中过滤可能更简单。
tradeoff: 预计算换查询速度 vs 缓存键数量和失效复杂度
optionExplanations: 放弃缓存每次全表扫描，250 组分类请求会持续压垮数据库，完全没有解决规模问题。
只支持一个分类是缩小产品范围来回避问题，不满足多分类的需求。
对，给每个 category-region 组合预建 sorted set，能把分类查询变成简单的 Redis 范围读取，代价是缓存键和维护复杂度都会增加。
把结构化字段藏进文件名里既没法被正常查询也没法索引，纯粹是取巧而不是设计。
optionExplanations_en: Rescanning the full table on every request lets the 250 category-region combinations keep hammering the database — it doesn't solve the scaling problem at all.
Supporting only one category shrinks the product scope to dodge the problem instead of meeting the multi-category requirement.
Right — building one sorted set per category-region pair turns every category page into a plain range lookup on Redis, though it does add extra keys and invalidation work to keep track of.
Hiding a structured field inside an image filename can't be queried or indexed properly — it's a workaround, not a design.

scenario: 希望支持分类 feed，但不想把同一篇文章复制到 250 个 category-region 缓存里。
scenario_en: You want category feeds, but you do not want to copy the same article into 250 category-region caches.
q: 更简单的缓存策略是什么？
q_en: What is the simpler caching strategy?
options: 给每一个活跃用户都建一个专属 category cache
所有分类请求一律都返回空列表结果
分类过滤功能只能放在数据库里做全文搜索
读取区域缓存最近 1000 篇，按 category 内存过滤
options_en: Build a dedicated category cache for every single active user.
Return an empty list result for every category request.
Handle category filtering only through database full-text search.
Read the latest 1,000 from the regional cache and filter by category in memory.
codeSample:
const articles = zrevrange('feed:US', 0, 999);
return articles.filter(a => a.category === 'sports').slice(0, 20);
why: 读取 1000 条热文章再内存过滤通常只需十几毫秒，避免了跨分类重复存储。
why_en: Reading a thousand hot articles and filtering in memory takes just milliseconds and avoids duplicating articles across category caches.
whenOtherWins: 如果长尾分类很稀疏，最近 1000 篇里经常凑不够结果，预计算分类 cache 更合适。
tradeoff: 内存过滤省缓存键 vs 预计算换取稳定命中量
optionExplanations: 给每个用户单独建分类缓存，用户量一大缓存条目会直接爆炸，成本比预计算还高。
分类请求一律返回空列表，分类功能等于形同虚设，没有满足产品需求。
把分类过滤全下放给数据库全文搜索，高频请求照样会持续打到数据库，没解决读压力。
对，复用区域缓存读最近 1000 篇再按 category 在内存过滤，通常只要十几毫秒，还避免了跨分类重复存储文章。
optionExplanations_en: Building a dedicated cache per user makes entry count explode as the user base grows — more expensive than precomputing by category.
Returning an empty list for every category request makes the feature effectively nonexistent — it doesn't meet the product requirement.
Pushing all category filtering onto database full-text search still leaves hot requests hammering the database — it doesn't relieve read pressure.

Right — pulling the latest 1,000 from the regional cache, then narrowing to one category inside the app process, adds only a few ms of extra work and sidesteps storing the same rows again across a dozen per-topic caches.

q: 预计算 category-region feed 和区域 cache 内存过滤的关键取舍是什么？
q_en: What is the key tradeoff between precomputed category-region feeds and in-memory filtering over a regional cache?
options: 前者不能用 Redis 实现，后者必须换成关系型数据库
前者只能给移动端用，后者只能给桌面端用，互不通用
两者在读延迟和内存占用上完全没有任何可衡量的差异
前者读更直接但内存和失效更复杂，后者更省内存但可能需要多取再过滤
options_en: Precompute cannot be built with Redis at all, so in-memory filtering must run on a relational database instead.
Precompute only works for mobile clients, and in-memory filtering only works for desktop clients, with no overlap.
The two approaches have no measurable difference at all in read latency or memory usage.
Precompute reads faster but costs more memory and invalidation work; in-memory filtering saves memory but may need overfetching.
why: 预计算牺牲内存和维护换极快读；内存过滤保留架构简单，但要求缓存里能凑够结果。
why_en: Precomputing trades memory and maintenance for the fastest reads, while in-memory filtering stays simpler but depends on the cache holding enough matches.
tradeoff: 预计算的读取速度 vs 内存过滤的架构简单
optionExplanations: 这编造了两者的技术限制，两种方案其实都能用 Redis 实现，不存在只能用数据库的限制。
这编造了平台限制，两种缓存策略跟客户端是移动端还是桌面端完全无关。
两者在延迟和内存上其实有真实差异，说没差异会让人忽略真正的成本取舍。
对，预计算换来更直接的读，代价是缓存键和失效更复杂；内存过滤省内存和维护，代价是可能要多取一批数据再过滤才够。
optionExplanations_en: This fabricates a technical limitation — both approaches can be built on Redis; there's no rule forcing the other one onto a database.
This fabricates a platform limitation — neither caching strategy has anything to do with whether the client is mobile or desktop.
The two really do differ in latency and memory footprint; claiming no difference hides the real cost tradeoff.

Right — precomputed sets read faster at the cost of extra memory and invalidation upkeep, while filtering the regional cache in memory stays leaner but sometimes has to pull extra rows before it finds a full page of results.

q: 请求时实时把数千篇文章和 100M 用户画像逐个打分，主要后果是什么？
q_en: What is the main consequence of scoring thousands of articles against 100M user profiles on each request?
options: Redis 内存占用会降为 0
所有用户都会自动强一致
发布方 webhook 不再需要认证
延迟和计算成本远超 200ms 目标
options_en: Redis memory usage magically drops to zero.
Every user automatically gets strong consistency.
Publisher webhooks no longer need authentication.
Latency and compute cost blow far past the 200ms target.
why: 实时给每个用户逐篇打分会把每次 feed 请求变成昂贵计算，流量尖峰时尤其失控。
why_en: Scoring every article against each user's profile in real time turns a feed request into expensive compute that spikes out of control under load.
optionExplanations: 打分方式的改变跟 Redis 内存占用没有关系，这个因果不成立。
一致性模型不受实时打分逻辑影响，两者是不同的设计维度。
webhook 认证是独立的安全机制，跟 feed 打分方式无关。
对，逐篇给每个用户实时算分，等于把一次简单的 feed 读请求变成一次昂贵的批量计算，一旦流量突增，延迟和账单会同时爆表。
optionExplanations_en: Changing how scoring works has no bearing on Redis memory usage — that causal link doesn't exist.
Consistency model is unaffected by real-time scoring logic; the two are different design dimensions entirely.
Webhook authentication is an independent security mechanism, unrelated to how the feed gets scored.

Right — running the whole article set through each reader's profile on every request turns a cheap feed read into a heavyweight computation, and under a traffic spike both latency and cost blow past target.

q: 给 5000 万活跃用户各存 1000 篇个性化 feed cache，主要问题是什么？
q_en: What is the main problem with storing 1,000 personalized cached articles for each of 50M active users?
options: 用户无法看到任何新闻
分类 feed 会自动消失
发布方不再需要 RSS
缓存条目规模会膨胀到数百亿级
options_en: Users are no longer able to see any news at all.
Category feeds automatically disappear.
Publishers no longer need to maintain RSS.
Cache entries balloon to tens of billions in total.
why: 专属用户 feed 读得快，但内存和更新成本会按用户数线性爆炸。
why_en: Per-user feeds read fast, but memory and update cost explode linearly with the number of active users.
optionExplanations: 用户仍然能看到自己的个性化 feed，只是背后的存储代价太大，功能本身没有消失。
分类 feed 是独立的缓存结构，不会因为个性化缓存的问题而自动消失。
RSS 采集跟这个缓存策略是两件事，发布方是否维护 RSS 不受影响。
对，5000 万用户乘以每人 1000 篇，条目数直接冲到数百亿级，内存和更新成本按用户数线性爆炸。
optionExplanations_en: Users still see their personalized feed just fine — the problem is the storage cost behind it, not the feature disappearing.
Category feeds are a separate cache structure; they don't vanish because of a personalized-cache problem elsewhere.
RSS ingestion is a separate concern from this caching strategy — publishers maintaining RSS is unaffected.
Right — multiply 50M users by 1,000 cached articles each and you land in the tens of billions of entries, with both footprint and refresh cost scaling straight-line with the user base.

scenario: 要在 100M 用户规模下提供个性化，又不能给每个用户维护 1000 条专属 cache。
scenario_en: At 100M users, the product wants personalization without maintaining a dedicated 1,000-item cache for every user.
q: 更平衡的方案是什么？
q_en: What is the more balanced personalization approach?
options: 每次请求都跑一遍完整推荐模型给所有文章打分
所有人永远只能看到同一个地区的 feed
为每一个用户各自复制一份全部文章
保存轻量用户偏好向量，按比例混合预计算分类 feed
options_en: Run the full recommendation model end to end and score every article on every single request.
Show every single user the exact same regional feed, forever, with zero personalization.
Duplicate the entire article set into a separate copy for every individual user.
Keep a lightweight preference vector per user and mix precomputed category feeds by ratio.
why: 用偏好向量混合技术、商业、趋势等分类 feed，内存只跟分类数和用户向量大小有关。
why_en: Mixing category feeds by a lightweight preference vector ties memory to the number of categories and a small per-user vector, not per-user feed copies.
whenOtherWins: 如果产品需要极深度推荐且流量较低，完整推荐服务和用户级预计算可能值得投入。
tradeoff: 轻量混合个性化 vs 深度推荐的更强相关性
diagram:
flowchart LR
Regional[Regional top stories] --> Ranker[Light ranker]
Profile[User profile] --> Ranker
Ranker --> Cache[Small user cache]
Cache --> Feed[Personalized feed]
optionExplanations: 每次请求都跑完整模型给海量文章打分，会重演实时打分那种延迟和成本失控的问题。
所有人看同一份地区 feed 等于彻底放弃了个性化，不满足产品目标。
给每个用户复制全部文章，存储成本比逐用户专属缓存还要夸张。
对，靠一个精简的偏好向量去按比例拼装已有的分类 feed，占用空间只取决于分类数量和向量本身大小，不会随用户规模线性变大。
optionExplanations_en: Running the full model to score every article on every request just reproduces the same latency and cost blowup as real-time scoring.
Showing everyone the same regional feed abandons personalization entirely — it doesn't meet the product goal.
Duplicating every article per user costs even more storage than a dedicated per-user cache would.
Right — blending the existing per-topic feeds by a compact set of per-user weights keeps footprint tied to how many topics exist plus one small vector per user, not a full copy per person.

q: 补全 Google News 的关键非功能目标：
q_en: Fill in the key nonfunctional targets for Google News:
text: 本题强调 {{availability}} 优先于严格一致，支持约 {{100M}} DAU 和更高峰值，feed 首屏加载目标小于 {{200ms}}。
why: 这些数字决定了后续必须做区域缓存、预计算和横向扩展。
why_en: These targets are why the design needs regional caching, precomputation, and horizontal scaling downstream.

scenario: 新闻聚合器只展示文章摘要和跳转链接，全文由发布方网站托管，不在平台内展示。
scenario_en: The news aggregator shows article summaries and outbound links; full text is hosted on publisher sites, not inside the platform.
q: 为什么新闻聚合器不需要 GET /article/{id}/content 这个接口？
q_en: Why does the news aggregator not need a GET /article/{id}/content endpoint?
options: 普通浏览器技术上不能打开外部网站
文章全文必须一直存在 Redis 里
点击这个行为一定被划在线下范围
平台是聚合器，客户端直接跳转到发布方 URL
options_en: A regular browser is technically unable to open an external website.
The full article text must permanently live inside Redis.
Click behavior is, by definition, always considered out of scope here.
The platform is an aggregator, so the client redirects straight to the publisher's URL.
why: 聚合器展示摘要和链接，全文由发布方网站托管，平台不需要托管全文接口。
why_en: An aggregator stores and shows metadata but sends the browser to the publisher for the full article, so it needs no content-hosting endpoint.
optionExplanations: 浏览器打开外部网站完全正常，这个技术限制不成立。
全文本就不该被平台存储，这个前提直接搞反了聚合器的设计。
点击追踪其实完全可以是一个线上功能，这个说法只是随口编造的限制。
对，平台的产品定位是聚合器，展示摘要后客户端直接跳到发布方 URL，平台不需要托管全文接口。
optionExplanations_en: Browsers open external sites all the time; there's no such technical limitation.
Full text shouldn't be stored by the platform at all — this premise gets the aggregator's design backwards.
Click tracking can absolutely be a live feature; this is just an invented restriction.

Right — this is an aggregator by design: once the summary shows, the client redirects the reader over to the source site for the rest, so there's no reason to build an endpoint that serves full article content.

scenario: 后续想统计文章点击并用于推荐训练，但仍要把用户送到发布方站点。
scenario_en: A later version wants click analytics for recommendation training while still sending users to the publisher site.
q: 应该如何改造点击路径？
q_en: How should the click path be changed?
options: 把每篇文章的全文内容都原样复制一份，存到本地服务器长期保留备份
永久禁用所有跳转到发布方站点的外部链接，一律不允许保留
让负责缓存的 Redis 服务反过来直接调用用户浏览器的接口
链接先到 /article/{id} 记录事件，再 302 跳转发布方
options_en: Copy the full text of every single article onto the local server and keep it as a permanent backup.
Permanently disable every outbound link to a publisher site, with no exceptions kept.
Have the Redis caching service reach back out and call the user's browser directly through its own interface.
Point the link at /article/{id} to log the event, then 302 redirect to the publisher.
why: 跟踪端点先记录 click event，再用 HTTP 302 完成跳转，不改变聚合器的产品定位。
why_en: A tracking endpoint logs the click event first, then issues an HTTP 302 redirect, without changing the aggregator's product shape.
whenOtherWins: 如果隐私或合规要求不允许点击追踪，直接外链更简单也收集更少数据。
tradeoff: 点击追踪支撑推荐 vs 直接外链的隐私简单

termDefinitions.meaning: HTTP 状态码，告诉浏览器改去另一个 URL 继续请求。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An HTTP 302 tells the browser to continue the request at a different URL.

optionExplanations: 把全文整份复制到自己服务器保存，会带来版权和存储成本的双重问题。
永久禁用跳转会让用户读不到全文，直接违反聚合器不托管全文的产品边界。
Redis 是缓存服务，没有能力也不该直接操作用户的浏览器，这个交互路径不成立。
对，链接先打到跟踪端点记录点击事件，再用标准 302 跳转到发布方，既拿到了推荐训练数据又没改变用户体验。
optionExplanations_en: Copying every article's full text onto the local server for good creates both a copyright problem and a storage cost problem.
Cutting off every outbound link for good means readers can never reach the source article, breaking the whole premise that this product doesn't host full text.
Redis is a caching service with no ability, and no business, to call a user's browser directly — that interaction path doesn't exist.

Right — the link hits a small tracking hop that records which article got clicked, followed by a normal 302 that carries the reader onward, so recommendation training gets its data without the user noticing any difference.

scenario: 新闻高峰期发布方每小时新增 50-100 篇文章，用户连续浏览 feed 10 分钟。
scenario_en: During a news peak, publishers add 50-100 articles per hour while a user browses the feed for 10 minutes.
q: 以这个发布速率，为什么 OFFSET 分页会很快明显漂移？
q_en: At this publish rate, why does OFFSET pagination drift quickly?
options: 数据库会在用户浏览的这几分钟内自动清空全部历史文章
客户端发出的分页 limit 参数会被服务器强制重置为零
RSS 抓取的速度快慢和分页机制的具体实现完全没有关系
浏览窗口内顶部很可能插入了新文章，offset 对不上
options_en: The database automatically clears every historical article during these few minutes.
The server forcibly resets the client's limit parameter to zero.
How fast RSS is fetched has nothing to do with how pagination is implemented.
New articles likely landed above the feed during the window, so the offset no longer lines up.
why: 几分钟内就可能有新文章插入 feed 顶部，offset 边界随之移动，用户翻页时会重复或跳过内容。
why_en: At this publish rate, several new articles can land above the current page within minutes, so offset boundaries drift and users see duplicates or gaps.
optionExplanations: 数据库不会因为用户在浏览就清空历史文章，这个假设凭空捏造。
limit 参数不会被服务器强制重置，这跟 offset 漂移毫无关系。
抓取速度恰恰决定了新文章进库的频率，跟分页漂移是不是很快出现直接相关，这个说法反而说反了。
对，每小时 50-100 篇的发布速率下，几分钟内顶部很可能已经插入了新文章，offset 边界跟着移动，翻页就会对不上。
optionExplanations_en: The database doesn't clear historical articles just because a user is browsing — that's a fabricated assumption.
The server doesn't forcibly reset the limit parameter; that has nothing to do with offset drift.
Fetch cadence is exactly what determines how quickly fresh stories appear, which is directly tied to how soon drift shows up — this claim gets the relationship backwards.
Right — at 50-100 stories an hour, odds are good that something new has slipped in ahead of what's on screen within just a few minutes, so the boundary the client is holding onto no longer lines up.

q: 补全发布方优先级轮询策略：
q_en: Fill in the publisher priority polling strategy:
text: 高频重大来源可以每 {{5-10 分钟}} 轮询，中等来源约 {{30 分钟}}，低频来源约 {{2-3 小时}}。
why: 优先级轮询把新鲜度预算花在真正高价值、高频发布的来源上。
why_en: Priority polling spends the freshness budget on the publishers that are actually high-value and high-frequency.

q: 把 CDC 更新区域 feed cache 的步骤排好序：
q_en: Put the CDC regional feed cache update steps in order:
steps: Worker 根据地区和相关性选择要更新的 feed key
Data Collection Service 将新文章写入数据库
Redis sorted set ZADD 新文章并裁剪最旧成员
数据库变更流产生 CDC 事件
why: CDC 让缓存更新跟随写入事件发生，而不是等读请求 miss 或 TTL 过期。
why_en: CDC drives cache updates from write events instead of waiting for a read miss or TTL expiry.
tradeoff: 事件驱动的即时刷新 vs 被动等待 miss/TTL 的简单实现
diagram:
flowchart TD
Article[New article] --> CDC[CDC event]
CDC --> Select[Find region feeds]
Select --> Insert[Prepend article id]
Insert --> Trim[Trim list]
Trim --> Serve[Serve from Redis]

q: 如果区域 Redis feed 里直接存文章 JSON 元数据，通常应包含哪些字段用于展示和过滤？（多选）
q_en: If the regional Redis feed stores article JSON metadata directly, which fields should it include for display and filtering? (Select all that apply.)
options: id、title、description/url
category、region、published_at
用户密码哈希
thumbnail URL 或媒体引用
options_en: id, title, and description/url.
category, region, and published_at.
the user's password hash.
a thumbnail URL or media reference.
why: 缓存 payload 应服务展示、分页和过滤；敏感用户字段不属于文章 feed cache。
why_en: Cached article payloads should serve display, pagination, and filtering, not carry sensitive user data.
optionExplanations: id、title、description/url 是渲染一条 feed 卡片必须的最基本字段，没有它们前端连展示都做不了。
category、region、published_at 三个字段撑起了分类过滤和按时间排序，是查询和展示都要用到的维度。
密码哈希是敏感用户凭证，混进文章 feed 缓存会造成不必要的数据泄露面，这个选项本身就是误判。
thumbnail URL 让客户端不用等文章详情接口就能先渲染出图片，是 feed 展示体验的一部分。
optionExplanations_en: id, title, and description/url are the bare minimum fields to render a feed card at all — without them the frontend can't display anything.
category, region, and published_at together power filtering by category and sorting by time — dimensions both queries and display rely on.
A password hash is an authentication secret with no display purpose; letting it ride along in an article feed cache just widens the blast radius if that cache ever leaks.
A thumbnail URL lets the client render the image without waiting on a separate article-detail call — part of the feed display experience.

q: 把 Google News 高质量方案的核心决策链排好序：
q_en: Put the core decision chain for a high-quality Google News design in order:
steps: 用 cursor 和单调 ID 避免无限滚动漂移
先采集发布方文章和缩略图，元数据入库、媒体入对象存储
用 CDC 预计算地区 Redis feed，读请求命中缓存
用 CDN 分发缩略图，区域部署和 Redis 读副本承接热点
按分类和偏好在缓存层过滤或组装，避免每次请求重算
why: 方案先满足基本采集和分页，再用预计算缓存、媒体 CDN、区域扩容和轻量个性化满足规模要求。
why_en: The final design first covers collection and pagination, then layers on precomputed caching, CDN media, regional scaling, and lightweight personalization for scale.
diagram:
flowchart LR
P[Publishers] --> C[Collection]
C --> DB[(Articles DB)]
C --> S3[(Object Storage)]
DB --> CDC[CDC]
CDC --> W[Feed Workers]
W --> R[(Regional Redis Feeds)]
S3 --> CDN[CDN]
R --> F[Feed Service]
CDN --> Client[Client]
F --> Client
